articles.name: How often does a web crawler check external content, and is it configurable?
articles.title: How often does a web crawler check external content, and is it configurable?
articles.body:
Question

For ZOS environment, how frequently does the new web crawler engine checks for new information and updates and is there a way to customize the frequency setting?

Answer

The web crawler runs automatically based on the syncing frequency configured in your Knowledge search settings, with options for Daily, Weekly, Monthly, or Never (defaulting to Weekly).

Also, please note:

  • The sitemap’s changefreq value does not affect the crawl schedule.
  • A crawl-delay directive in the site’s robots.txt file is not respected by the crawler.
  • If a scheduled crawl cannot complete—for example, because the website is temporarily unavailable—the previously indexed content remains searchable, and Zendesk will retry periodically.

Frequency of web crawler recrawls when changes are made directly on a customer's website

Several updates to the web crawler include the ability to customize the frequency of the crawler: daily, weekly, monthly or never (just like AI Agents). Frequency is not impacted by any plan or operational factors. Admins can customize the syncing frequency for both new and existing crawlers directly in Knowledge search settings. 

When the crawl status is “partially completed,” it indicates that some pages set for crawling were not indexed for reasons such as page errors, access issues, timeouts, exceeding limits, or content not being detected.  In this case you may review the crawler summary or contact Zendesk Customer Support for troubleshooting help.

articles.name: Can authenticated end-user names be displayed in conversations logs?
articles.title: Can authenticated end-user names be displayed in conversations logs?
articles.body:
Question

Can authenticated end-user names be displayed instead of “Customer” in the AI Agent Conversation Logs when authentication is enabled?

Answer

This is not possible right now. The system currently shows Customer for both authenticated and unauthenticated users in the Conversation logs for AI Agents. You will only find the customer's name visible on the related Zendesk ticket.

articles.name: Can we enable AI agents to remember previous replies/conversations, feedback etc.?
articles.title: Can we enable AI agents to remember previous replies/conversations, feedback etc.?
articles.body:
Question

Regarding Memory-rich AI, can we enable AI agents to remember previous replies/conversations, feedback etc.?

Answer

Zendesk AI agents can remember previous interactions, replies, and feedback within an active conversation, enabling natural, context-aware, and adaptive responses. However, "memory" in this context is session-based and does not mean agents persistently track a user's full support history across separate conversations by default.

articles.name: An entity wasn't recognized in email conversations with AI
articles.title: An entity wasn't recognized in email conversations with AI
articles.body:
Issue symptom

I noticed that an entity wasn't recognized in conversations, named Order_Number and another REGEX entity. Customer needs help with order number entities not being recognized in email bot (AI agent).

Resolution

It's possible that:

  1. You updated the regex used for Order_Number in the entity after the conversation you looked at were created. For example, conversation examples were created on August 7th and 9th. However, your entities were updated on August 12th.

  2. In addition, it's an expected behavior that Regex entities would never match in some conversations. The Regex used in the entity expects the order ID to start with 1 followed by seven digits. If the order IDs in the conversation examples do not have that pattern, no match is possible.

articles.name: Is there a limit to the number of steps in the generative procedures of an email AI agent?
articles.title: Is there a limit to the number of steps in the generative procedures of an email AI agent?
articles.body:
Question

Is there a maximum number of steps in the generative procedures of an email bot? My procedure needs to acknowledge additions and changes for more than 6 steps, but the flow is only built up to the fourth step. The procedure should have more than 6 steps, but the flow only has 4 steps. How can I reach my goal?

Answer

No, there's no set limit to the number of steps in generative procedures for email AI agents.

If your procedure needs more than the initial four steps shown in the map:

  1. You can keep adding steps by using the free-text adjustment field in the procedure builder and selecting Update procedure.

  2. The system will update the map each time you make changes, so you can repeat this process until your procedure is complete.

articles.name: Understanding how Explore calculates metrics and why similar report results might not match
articles.title: Understanding how Explore calculates metrics and why similar report results might not match
articles.body:
When a number in an Explore report doesn’t match what you expect or if it differs from another report, there might be a mismatch between what you think you are measuring and what you are actually measuring. The difference may be caused by the dataset, metric, filters, date range, aggregation, or time settings.

What's my plan?
All Suites Professional, Enterprise, or Enterprise Plus
Support with Explore Professional or Enterprise

Summary: ◀▼

Learn how report metrics are calculated so you can spot why similar Explore reports differ. The article explains how datasets, filters, date ranges, aggregation, time zones, business or calendar hours, and ticket changes like merges, deletions, and reopens can affect results. It also helps you compare averages, medians, and ticket status-based time metrics when numbers don’t match expectations.

When a number in an Explore report doesn’t match what you expect or if it differs from another report, there might be a mismatch between what you think you are measuring and what you are actually measuring. The difference may be caused by the dataset, metric, filters, date range, aggregation, or time settings.

This article explains at a high level how metrics work, how time-based metrics are measured, and how ticket changes impact reports. Having a better understanding of how things are measured and knowing what to look for, can help ensure your reports are consistent. It can also help you resolve mismatches or discrepancies between your expectations and your reports.

This article contains the following topics:

  • Understanding how metrics work and the parts of a report
  • Understanding how time-based metrics are measured in reports
  • Understanding how ticket changes impact reports and why numbers change
  • Summary of what to check when results don’t match expectations

Related articles

  • Metrics and attributes for Zendesk Support
  • Understanding datasets
  • Data refresh intervals for analytics
  • Understanding discrepancies between Explore reports and exports

Understanding how metrics work and the parts of a report

A metric is a measure, such as the number of tickets or the time to first reply. Explore applies an aggregation to the metric, such as count, sum, average, or median, to calculate the result. Metrics are retrieved from a dataset containing your Zendesk data.

If two or more similar reports return different results, any of the following might be different in the reports:
  • Datasets
  • Metrics or metric formulas
  • Filters or Date attributes
  • Aggregations
  • Types of records, such as tickets or ticket updates

Before investigating a difference, check that both reports use the same dataset, metrics, filters, and time zone settings.

Understanding how time-based metrics are measured in reports

Time-based metrics measure specific periods in a ticket’s lifecycle. They don’t all measure the same kind of waiting time. For example, first reply time measures the time from ticket creation to the first public agent reply, while requester wait time measures the time a ticket spends in the New, Open, and On-hold statuses.

If you're seeing discrepancies between your time-based reports, check the following:

  • In which statuses is duration counted?: Some metrics, such as Requester wait time measure time in specific requester-facing statuses. The time an agent spends working might be excluded by design. Check which ticket statuses the metric includes. For example, requester wait time includes time in the New, Open, and On-hold statuses and does not display data for any other ticket status.

    You can create a report using your chosen metric and the Ticket status attribute to help you see which statuses a specific status measures.

    See the following articles for more information about time-based metrics:

    • About native Support time duration metrics
    • About native Call time duration metrics
  • Business vs calendar hours: Many time metrics exist in both business and calendar time variants which give different results. Check which one your report uses and whether your schedules are configured.

    When you create a report, time-based metrics are clearly labelled as using business or calendar hours.

  • Averages can hide distribution: Averages can be affected by unusually high or low values. Compare the average and median when you want to understand whether a small number of tickets is influencing the result. The average shows the overall mean; the median shows the middle value when the results are ordered. See Choosing metric aggregators.

Make sure you understand the definitions for first reply time, full resolution time, requester wait time, and agent work time. See Explore metrics.

Understanding how ticket changes impact reports and why numbers change

Explore reflects the current state of your ticket history. When tickets are updated, merged, or deleted, metrics computed over that history change retrospectively. In addition, recently closed activity can take time to appear while data syncs. This is expected behavior, but it means a screenshot of last month’s report is not a reliable baseline for validating today’s report.

Understanding the behavior of merged, deleted, and closed tickets can help you understand the results you see in your reports and potentially solve any discrepancies between your reports. Check for the following:
  • Merged tickets: A merged ticket is closed and its conversation moves to a new ticket. Merging a ticket can affect reports because the original ticket and the ticket it was merged into may no longer represent separate conversations. Check the dataset and metric definition to understand how merged tickets are counted.
  • Deleted tickets: Deleted tickets aren’t included in the Tickets dataset. As a result, a report can return a different result if tickets were deleted after an earlier report was run.
  • Solved date versus updated-date: Some metrics use when an event occurred, while others use the ticket’s current state. For example, a report filtered by Ticket solved - Date may include tickets solved during the selected period, while the Solved tickets metric counts tickets that are currently solved or closed. A ticket that was solved and later reopened can therefore affect these reports differently.

Summary of what to check when results don’t match expectations

If results in your reports don’t match your expectations or if you see discrepancies among reports, you can check the following:

  • Are both reports using the same dataset,?
  • Are both reports using the same filters (including hidden or default filters) and the same date attributes?
  • Are both reports using the same metric, metric formula, and aggregation? For example, are both using average rather than median, or count rather than distinct count?
  • Are both reports using the same metric, metric formula, and aggregation? For example, are both using average rather than median, or count rather than distinct count?
  • If you're comparing reports generated by different users make sure that they have the same time zone and start of the week (based on the language of the user)
  • Are both reports using the same hours measurement. For example, is one report using calendar hours and the other using business hours?
  • Were any tickets merged, deleted, reopened, or otherwise changed during or after the report period?

If you still don’t understand your results or if the numbers still differ significantly after you’ve completed your checklist, contact Zendesk Customer Support and include:

  • The exported report or a screen recording
  • The dataset name
  • The exact metric, including its formula from the Metrics panel
  • Two or three example ticket IDs

articles.name: Scheduled Maintenance -  October 5-20, 2026 - Pod 15 - Analytics Data Migration
articles.title: Scheduled Maintenance -  October 5-20, 2026 - Pod 15 - Analytics Data Migration
articles.body:
Zendesk will perform critical maintenance which will impact data freshness for customers on Pod 15 at some time between October 5th and 20th.
 

Important Note

During this maintenance window, analytics and reporting data for Pod 15 accounts will not refresh. Real-time monitoring, live agent activity, and core support operations are not affected. No data will be lost. The change moves the analytics data hosting from the United States to Australia to support in-country data residency for Australian customers.
 

What is happening

Zendesk is migrating Pod 15 analytics data from our US instance to a new Australia-based instance. This is part of our investment in data locality for Australian customers, enabling analytics data to be hosted in-country.

To perform the migration safely, we need to pause writes of new analytics data to the current US instance, migrate the historical and new data to Australia, validate it, and then reconnect analytics services to the Australian instance. During this transition, some analytics and reporting features will show data that is not current.
 

Maintenance window

This window avoids end-of-month reporting and billing cycles. The migration cannot be rescheduled per customer - it is a coordinated Pod-wide cutover.
 

What is affected

The following analytics and reporting features will not refresh with new data during the window:

  • Explore: 8 of 29 datasets will show data that is not current. The affected datasets are:
    • Knowledge - Quick Answers
    • Knowledge - User session
    • Knowledge - Page efficiency
    • Chat - Messaging Goal Conversions
    • AI Agents - Essential
    • AI - Intelligent Triage
    • AI - Copilot auto assist
    • AI - Copilot suggestions
    • The remaining 21 Explore datasets continue to refresh normally.
  • HyperArc (Agentic Analytics): Analytics data will not refresh during the window.
  • OBP usage dashboards (Admin Center): Detailed usage drill-down tables will be temporarily hidden. The total consumption figure and summary tiles remain visible and accurate.
  • Automated Resolution forecasts: Forecast notifications may be based on data that is not current during the window. Other real-time usage notifications are not affected.
  • ZQA dashboards (Quality Assurance): Customer-facing analytics dashboards will show data frozen at the last refresh before the window. The "Last updated time" indicator on each dashboard shows when data was last refreshed.
     

What is NOT affected

  • Real-time monitoring (ZRA) - live agent activity, real-time analytics, and live dashboards continue to operate normally
  • Core support operations - ticketing, messaging, talk, chat, and agent workflows are fully operational
  • Historical data - all existing analytics data remains accessible
  • Billing and usage totals - total consumption figures remain accurate
  • 21 of 29 Explore datasets - refresh normally throughout
     

What customers need to do

  • No configuration changes are required.
  • If you have access to HyperArc but have not yet enabled it, please wait until after this maintenance window before enabling it, to avoid a confusing experience with non-current data.
  • After the window completes, allow time for data to backfill and validate. Reports and dashboards will return to normal refresh rates once the migration is complete and validated.
     

What to expect during the window

  • Dashboards and reports for affected features will display data that is not current, frozen at the last refresh before the migration began.
  • No error messages will be shown - dashboards remain accessible, but the data will not reflect recent activity.
  • Once the migration is complete and validated, all affected analytics services will reconnect to the Australian instance and resume normal refresh rates.
     

Why we are doing this

This migration enables Zendesk to host Pod 15 analytics data in Australia, supporting data locality requirements for Australian customers in regulated industries. After completion, analytics data for Pod 15 accounts will be stored in-country.
 

Questions or concerns

If you have questions, please contact Zendesk Support or your account representative. For status updates during the maintenance window, refer to status.zendesk.com.

articles.name: How can I set up geo blocking for my AI agent?
articles.title: How can I set up geo blocking for my AI agent?
articles.body:
Question

Can I set up geo blocking for my AI agent or bot widget? I'd like to set up geo blocking, so the French bot only appears to users with a French IP address for example. Is this possible?

Answer

No, you cannot block users geographically with AI agent and messaging settings.

Workarounds

However, you can use these workarounds instead:

Conditionally load the widget on the website

  • What it does: The customer’s site can perform an IP-geolocation check, then only inject/load the Zendesk widget for visitors located in France or another country

  • Considerations: Requires custom development and an IP geolocation provider or service, outside of your Zendesk configuration

Use CDN or WAF geo rules

  • What it does: Configure geographic restriction rules at your CDN or Web Application Firewall (WAF) level to filter traffic or restrict widget access based on visitor IP location at the network edge.

  • Considerations: This is best for stricter geographic controls, but is outside Zendesk configuration

Separate French language site or brand page

  • What it does: Add the French or language widget only to the French or language version of the site

  • Considerations: This is straightforward if you already have language or region-specific pages

articles.name: Announcing saved recommendations in admin copilot
articles.title: Announcing saved recommendations in admin copilot
articles.body:
We’re excited to announce that you can now save recommendations for later in admin copilot.

This announcement includes the following topics:

  • What is changing?
  • Why is Zendesk making this change?
  • What do I need to do?

What is changing?

You can now save admin copilot recommendations you want to revisit.

When a recommendation is useful but you’re not ready to act on it, you can save it for later and find it in a dedicated tab on the Recommendations page in Admin Center. This makes it easier to keep track of valuable opportunities without interrupting the work you're currently focused on.

Why is Zendesk making this change?

Saving recommendations for later gives you more control over when you act on recommendations. It helps you:

  • Keep useful recommendations in view while focusing on higher-priority work.
  • Return to a focused list when you’re ready to review or implement recommendations.
  • Distinguish between recommendations that are valuable but not timely and those that are less relevant.

Saved recommendations also give admin copilot a clearer signal about what you find useful, which helps Zendesk improve the relevance of future recommendations over time.

What do I need to do?

No immediate action is required. This new feature will be available automatically in your account. To learn more, see Optimizing your account with admin copilot insights and recommendations.

articles.name: Why does an AI agent reply on an email ticket fulfill the first reply time SLA?
articles.title: Why does an AI agent reply on an email ticket fulfill the first reply time SLA?
articles.body:
Question

Why does the first reply time (FRT) SLA appear as met when an AI agent sends the first public reply on an email ticket?

Answer

This is expected behavior. For email channel tickets, an AI agent public reply can fulfill the first reply time (FRT) SLA target. In SLA reporting, that AI-generated public reply is treated as the first reply on the ticket, so the first reply time target may appear as achieved immediately.

This can be confusing because SLAs don't apply to AI agent tickets which refers specifically to conversations handled entirely by messaging or voice AI agents. Those are different from email channel tickets where an AI agent is connected to the email channel and sends a public reply.

What you can expect in reports

If the AI agent posts the first public reply on an email channel ticket:

  • the SLA First Reply Time target may show as Achieved
  • the SLA metric for the first reply time may appear as 0 minutes or near-immediate

For more information on how the first reply time is calculated, see Understanding ticket reply time.

articles.name: Release notes through 2026-09-04
articles.title: Release notes through 2026-09-04
articles.body:
See the What's New section for an overview of what was released last month.

This week's release notes include:

  • Knowledge and AI agents
  • Voice
  • Apps and integrations
  • Products with no updates this week

Knowledge and AI agents

AI Agents: 

New:
  • Agentic Messaging: If a customer's request still isn't clear after two clarifying questions, the agent escalates to a human agent rather than continuing to ask, preventing conversations from stalling in endless back-and-forth.
Fixed:
  • Agentic Messaging: Smoother handoffs after a flow ends. When a procedure completes, the agent now waits for the customer's next message instead of automatically jumping back in with a generic "how can I help you?" If the customer has other open requests queued, the agent will still proactively move on to the next one.
  • Agentic Email: procedures can now accurately reproduce long JWT/base64 links without the LLM dropping characters.

Knowledge: 

Fixed:

  • Restoring an older article revision no longer incorrectly offers save and migrate.
  • Waiting for the editor's node transformation prevents caption changes from reverting to plain text. 

Help Center

Fixed:

  • Help Center now uses plural forms for “more articles” and request counts, and the preview bar handles right-to-left layouts correctly.

Voice

New:

  • Added a new call leg status: "Agent unreachable", along with a new metric called "Unreachable call legs." This metric tracks call legs that didn't ring because agents couldn't be reached, such as when their browser or Zendesk tab was closed, or due to network issues. This helps customers distinguish between genuinely missed calls (when the call rings but isn't answered) and cases where the agent could not have answered because they were unreachable (such as a closed browser or network disruptions that prevent the call from connecting). 

Apps and integrations

New:
  • Rules Analysis by AgentCopilot (Support)
    • Rules Analysis gives Zendesk admins a single-page audit of every trigger, automation, and shared macro in their account — flagging the ones that are silently broken. Rules quietly decay as fields get deactivated, groups get renamed, and dropdown values disappear. Broken rules keep running but stop doing what they should — tickets route to the wrong queue, macros set values that no longer exist, automations fire without effect. Rules Analysis surfaces it all at a glance.
  • Keito (Support) 
    • Keito brings project-based time tracking into Zendesk Support. Agents connect their own Keito account, choose a project and task, then start or stop a timer directly from the ticket sidebar. The app shows the agent's time and the team's total time for the current ticket.
  • CXConnect (Support)
    • CXConnect enables Zendesk Support agents and administrators to send proactive WhatsApp campaigns and notifications directly from Zendesk — without leaving the platform. All messages are delivered through Sunshine Conversations (Sunco), ensuring full compliance with WhatsApp Business API standards and complete conversation traceability inside Zendesk tickets.
  • Conditional Dropdown Filter (Support)
    • Conditional Dropdown Filter lets admins connect two dropdown ticket fields so that when an agent selects a value in the parent field, the child field instantly shows only the relevant options.
  • Holy Grail AI Agent (Support)
    • Holy Grail is a no-code platform for building enterprise-grade AI assistants — chatbots, e-mail assistants, and agent co-pilots — that companies can deploy without writing a single line of code.  The Zendesk integration brings Holy Grail's AI agents directly into the support workflow. Deflect repetitive tickets with an AI chatbot trained on their own knowledge sources, draft and auto-respond to incoming e-mail tickets with full context from Zendesk, equip agents with a co-pilot that suggests answers, summarizes threads, and pulls from connected knowledge bases, and auto-resolve tickets end-to-end when the AI's confidence score exceeds a customer-defined threshold 
  • Thread (Support) 
    • Thread is an agentic customer success platform from Thread Solution Inc. CS teams use Thread to automate onboarding, track customer health, and take action across the tools they already use. Connect your Zendesk in minutes: enter your subdomain, approve the OAuth consent screen, done. From then on, Thread's CSMs and AI agents can ground their work in your customers' real support experience.
  • Sola (Support)
    • Sola is an AI-native automation platform that helps enterprises build intelligent agents for repetitive, multi-step work beyond traditional RPA. The Sola integration connects authorized Zendesk Support accounts to Sola workflows. Users can retrieve tickets, update ticket fields and status, add public replies or internal notes, and upload files. Administrators can also configure custom Zendesk API requests. These actions can be combined with other Sola steps to automate support operations while keeping the connected account and selected action explicit in each workflow.
  • Holiday Greetings for Talk (Support) (paid)
    • Temporary holiday greetings take a few steps to set up and a few more to undo. This app puts all your holiday greetings in one place — and switches them on and off for you. Pick a holiday, or set your own dates and times. Choose your Talk lines, record or upload your greetings, and set the start and end. When the holiday starts, your holiday greetings go live. When it ends, your original greetings come back, exactly as they were — no morning-after cleanup. The app double-checks every change against Zendesk and emails you a confirmation when your greeting goes live and again when your original is restored — you never have to wonder.

Products with no updates this week

  • Admin Center
  • Support
  • Copilot
  • Analytics
  • Contact Center
  • Zendesk Workforce Management (WFM)
  • Zendesk QA
  • Mobile SDKs

articles.name: How can I remove a single brand from an automation?
articles.title: How can I remove a single brand from an automation?
articles.body:
Question

I need help with removing an automation. How can I ensure I only remove that automation for the brand of my team? At the moment, the automation does not reference our brand, but the business rule still captures our tickets.

Answer

To exclude your brand from an automation, add a nullifying condition to that brand:

  1. Edit the automation
  2. Under Meet all of the following conditions, add: Ticket: Brand | Is not | And the name of your brand
  3. Save your changes

articles.name: Why AI may use use case procedures differently across different languages
articles.title: Why AI may use use case procedures differently across different languages
articles.body:
Issue symptoms

I notice that my use case procedure is consistently matched by an AI agent in English, but the same procedure is not triggered as reliably in another language or locale, such as French. Even when the customer question appears to be a translation of the English version, the AI agent may interpret the phrasing differently and match it to another procedure instead.

Root cause

This can happen when the translated question is not close enough in meaning or wording to the phrasing your procedure is optimized to match. In English, the request may strongly align with a specific procedure, while in another language the translated phrasing may overlap more closely with a different procedure.

Resolution steps

To improve matching across languages, review the use case name and Reason for request and expand them to better reflect the phrasing customers are likely to use in each supported language. Including wording that more closely matches the translated intent can help AI agents identify and trigger the correct procedure more consistently.

Example procedure reason for request update

Original version

Procedure name: Usage fees refund requests

Reason for request: Customer mentions having been charged for a ride or a trip, and wanting a refund or a credit.

Improved version

Procedure name: Usage fees refund requests

Reason for request: Customer mentions being charged for a ride or trip and wants a refund or credit. This can include direct refund requests as well as questions about how, where, or what email address to use to submit a refund request. For example, if a customer asks where to write for a refund or how to request one, that can still be treated as a refund request rather than only an information request.

For more information, see Creating use cases for AI agents to identify what customers are asking about.

articles.name: Why aren’t my AI agent segments working with a custom user field?
articles.title: Why aren’t my AI agent segments working with a custom user field?
articles.body:
Question

I created a custom user field to store each customer’s VIP level. In AI agents, at the conversation started level, I added an action to get user metadata, entered the custom field, and saved the value as a parameter. I then used that parameter in my segments, but the setup still doesn’t work as expected.

Why aren’t my segments working in AI agents when I’m using a custom user field for a customer’s VIP level?

Answer

Segments in AI agents work with session parameters, not directly with custom user fields. If the VIP value is stored only in a custom user field, the segment won’t match unless that value is first passed into the session.

To configure this correctly:

  1. Capture the VIP level in chat metadata, widget metadata, or through an API integration
  2. Use the Get User action to save that value as a session parameter
  3. Verify that the session parameter exists and that its value matches the value your segment expects
  4. In the AI agents workspace, create or edit the segment using that session parameter
  5. If you’re using email AI agents, apply the segment at the use case level rather than inside a procedure

In short, the segment must evaluate a session parameter. Referencing a custom user field alone isn’t enough.

For more information, see Gathering and managing metadata for Sunshine Conversations and AI agents.

articles.name: Why are late customer replies not added to email AI agent conversation logs after 72 hours?
articles.title: Why are late customer replies not added to email AI agent conversation logs after 72 hours?
articles.body:
Question

When using the email AI agent, the AI agent may reply to ask the customer for more information. If the customer responds more than 72 hours later, their reply may appear on the ticket but not in the original AI agent conversation log.

  • Why are delayed customer replies not added to the AI agent conversation log after 72 hours?
  • In some cases, the ticket events also show the resolution type as Automated, even though the customer replied later. Why does this happen, and can this behavior be changed?

Answer

This behavior is expected.

If an end user does not reply within 72 hours of the AI agent’s latest message, the conversation may be classified as an automated resolution after a system verification step is completed by a large language model (LLM).

Once that happens:

  • The conversation is counted as an automated resolution
  • The automated resolution status cannot be reversed or changed
  • If the customer replies later, their message can still appear on the ticket itself, but it will not be added back into the original AI agent conversation log

How the 72-hour window works

The 72-hour period is based on end-user inactivity after the AI agent’s most recent message. For example, if the AI agent asks the customer for more details and the customer does not reply within the next 72 hours, the conversation may be marked as an automated resolution once the verification step is complete.

Can the 72-hour window be changed?

No. The 72-hour timeframe is part of the product’s current system behavior and is not configurable.

For more information, see:

  • About the automated resolutions platform (prior to resolution tiers)
  • About automated resolution tiers

articles.name: Service Incident - August 19, 2026 - Support | All Pods - Failures for 3rd-party apps
articles.title: Service Incident - August 19, 2026 - Support | All Pods - Failures for 3rd-party apps
articles.body:
Summary

On August 19, 2026, from 06:27 UTC and 08:09 UTC, some customers using third-party apps and certain Support apps across all Pods experienced app failures, 503 errors, and request timeouts. Contact Center login and integration functionality was also impacted.
 

Timeline

August 19, 2026 08:00 AM UTC 
We’re investigating an issue affecting third-party app functionality, where some customers may be unable to use certain apps or may encounter errors and timeouts. Our teams have observed that service is now operating normally. Please refresh your browser and check whether the issue has been resolved on your end. Thank you for your patience as we worked through this.
 
August 19, 2026 08:33 AM UTC
We’re happy to report that the issue affecting third-party app functionality has been fully resolved and service has been restored. We appreciate your understanding and cooperation throughout this incident.
 

Root Cause Analysis

This incident was caused by a configuration change that affected how requests from third-party apps were routed, resulting in 503 errors and timeouts.

The incident was made more difficult to diagnose by other changes occurring around the same time, as well as gaps in review and testing for the configuration change.
 

Resolution

To resolve the issue, we restored the affected request-routing configuration and validated recovery through automated testing, additional checks, and customer confirmation. We also restored related Contact Center configuration after a customer reported login and integration problems.

Customers were updated through the status page and support communications, with guidance to reload and re-check their apps where necessary.
 

Remediation Items

  1. Strengthen review and testing requirements for routing and configuration changes.
  2. Improve safeguards and lifecycle management for configuration changes.
  3. Improve change visibility and coordination during deployments.
  4. Continue enhancing monitoring and automated tests for app availability and routing.
  5. Document response and recovery procedures for future incidents.
     

FOR MORE INFORMATION

For current system status information about Zendesk and specific impacts to your account, visit our system status page. If you have additional questions about this incident, contact Zendesk customer support.

articles.name: Can my agentic email AI agent handle multiple intents and entity IDs?
articles.title: Can my agentic email AI agent handle multiple intents and entity IDs?
articles.body:
Question

Can my agentic email AI agent handle multiple intents? I am curious about the multi-intent capabilities of my AI agent, specifically around how Zendesk handles multiple entities.

For example, a customer emails me asking to cancel their trip and provides three different booking IDs in the same message.

Answer

Can an agentic email AI agent recognize multiple intents?

No. AI agents on email currently cannot process multiple procedure intents or perform parallel procedure automation within a single email reply, though they can answer multiple questions from knowledge sources.

Can the AI agent handle and process multiple intents, or only the first?

Only the first. While entity recognition can extract entity values such as booking IDs from a message, the AI agent works with a single entity value per procedure run and does not currently process multiple procedure intents at once.

  • In practice, this means it will pick up one booking ID, typically the first one it identifies, and proceed with that
  • Additional booking IDs in the same message won't each be processed as separate actions

Can the cancellation workflow loop through all three? What is the intended behavior for partial successes?

No. Currently, there is no built-in loop or a mechanism for each loop in conversation flows that would let a single procedure iterate over multiple values of the same entity.

  • The flow runs once, using the one booking ID it captured, performs the cancellation step, for example an API call, and replies
  • To cancel multiple bookings, each one must be handled as a separate run, either through additional back-and-forth with the customer or via a single API action on your side that accepts a list of IDs if your integration supports that

articles.name: My AI agent changes to English when there isn't enough text
articles.title: My AI agent changes to English when there isn't enough text
articles.body:
Issue symptoms

When I test the email AI agent for my bot, at Conversation starts, the procedure correctly detects the incoming language. However, the language changes to English when there is not sufficient context in any of the replies. This is under my bot with the use case Subscription Cancellation.

Root cause

This happens because the email AI agent falls back to its configured default language when the incoming message does not contain sufficient text for high-confidence language detection. The following behaviors are expected based on how language detection works:

  • AI agents determine customer language through natural language processing on the first message, CRM integration actions, or user selection in welcome messages. Language detection does not look up or fall back to user profile languages unless an action is explicitly configured to fetch customer locale from your CRM.
  • Opening and closing lines for email responses aren't translated automatically, so you need to provide versions for each language you support
  • The first message from the customer may be too short for the system to confidently match a language. As a result, the bot starts responding in the default language. This is expected behavior.
  • Language detection only runs when the active_language session parameter is empty (such as on the first message or after a language reset). Once active_language is set, the AI agent will not re-run language detection or automatically switch languages on subsequent emails unless the parameter is manually reset using an action.

Resolution steps

Short messages may always result in undetected languages.

To resolve this issue:

  1. Add the target language > activate that language for the AI agent
  2. Add custom email opening and closing lines in that language under Email content, and select Enable
  3. Confirm that your use case has content in the target language

For more information, see Configuring language detection for AI agents.

articles.name: About real-time voice translation in Contact Center (closed EAP)
articles.title: About real-time voice translation in Contact Center (closed EAP)
articles.body:
Real-time voice translation enables Contact Center agents and customers to communicate in different languages during a live voice call. Each call participant speaks in their preferred language and hears an AI-generated translation of the other participant's speech.

What's my plan?
Add-on Contact Center

Summary: ◀▼

Real-time voice translation lets you handle live voice calls in different languages, with you and the customer speaking your preferred languages while AI translates in the call. It can help you expand language coverage, reduce reliance on multilingual staffing or interpreters, and route calls by need instead of language fluency. It’s a closed EAP for Native Contact Center accounts with language, call-type, and usage limits.

Real-time voice translation is available through a closed Early Access Program (EAP). This feature is in development and is subject to change. To discuss eligibility and participation, contact your Zendesk account executive or customer success manager.

Real-time voice translation enables Contact Center agents and customers to communicate in different languages during a live voice call. Each call participant speaks in their preferred language and hears an AI-generated translation of the other participant's speech.

The feature can help businesses expand language coverage, make better use of their existing agents, and reduce their reliance on language-specific queues, multilingual staffing, and interpreters.

This article contains the following topics:

  • Understanding real-time voice translation
  • How real-time voice translation works
  • Requirements and limitations
  • Is this EAP right for your organization?
  • Joining the closed EAP

Understanding real-time voice translation

Real-time voice translation is designed for contact centers that support customers in different languages or have unpredictable demand for multilingual service. Agents can handle calls in supported languages without speaking the customer's language, so calls can be routed based on the customer's needs and the agent's expertise rather than language fluency alone.

Real-time voice translation is built into the Contact Center experience, enabling agents to manage translated calls alongside their existing call controls and workflows.

How real-time voice translation works

Translation can be configured before a call reaches an agent or enabled by an agent during a call.

Configuring translation before the call reaches an agent

Administrators can configure translation in a contact flow. The customer's language can be determined by the contact flow, a voice AI agent, or another pre-agent workflow.

When translation is configured before the call is connected:

  • The customer's language is set before the call is connected to an agent.
  • The agent is notified before answering that the call will be translated.
  • The agent and customer can speak in their preferred languages.

Configuring translation during a call

If a language was not set before the agent accepts the call, the agent can enable translation during the call when they determine that it would help the customer. Agents can also stop translation when it is no longer needed.

Requirements and limitations

The following requirements and limitations apply during the EAP:

  • Real-time voice translation is available only for Native Contact Center accounts.
  • Supported languages are Chinese, English, French, German, Hindi, Indonesian, Italian, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese, Russian, Spanish, and Vietnamese.
  • Multi-party calls, transferred calls, monitor or barge scenarios, and video calls are not supported when real-time voice translation is enabled.
  • Translation quality and latency can vary depending on the language, audio quality, accents, and network conditions.
  • Usage is subject to EAP limits.

Real-time voice translation produces AI-generated translations. Agents should use their judgment and follow their organization's policies when handling translated conversations.

Is this EAP right for your organization?

Real-time voice translation might be a good fit for your organization if you:

  • Receive voice calls from customers who speak different languages.
  • Have difficulty recruiting or scheduling multilingual agents.
  • Use language-specific queues or rely on interpreters.
  • Want to expand language coverage without building specialist teams for every language.
  • Have fluctuating or unpredictable multilingual demand.

The EAP might not be suitable if your organization requires translation for multi-party, transferred, monitored, barged, or video calls.

Joining the closed EAP

To join the closed EAP, contact your Zendesk account executive or customer success manager. They can help you confirm eligibility and coordinate enablement.

As an EAP participant, you must provide structured feedback and join regular feedback sessions. After your account is enabled, configure the relevant contact flows and language settings, train your agents, and test calls before using translation with customers.

articles.name: AI agent: My procedure skips multiple steps or follows the wrong decision-tree branch
articles.title: AI agent: My procedure skips multiple steps or follows the wrong decision-tree branch
articles.body:
Issue symptoms

With my AI agent and messaging, I create a Sunshine Conversations (SunCo) action with Get User, which retrieves the externalId field and saves it as externalId. However, with that parameter, the procedure skips multiple steps or follows the wrong decision-tree branch.

Resolution steps

The user information, especially the value of externalId, might be cached and available for retrieval. The AI agent then fails to set the parameters in the conversation, even though SunCo actions trigger to do so. Because externalId isn't present as a session parameter, the procedure takes this route. This means the procedure works correctly based on the session parameter information it can or can't access.

As a best practice, use the Conversation action to Set a new parameter with the value previously set by the SunCo action:

  • Collect parameters using SunCo actions

  • Reset the values by using another conversation action at the start of the conversation

  • Don't set more than one parameter with the same key. For example, in AI agent actions, don't set the value of externalId to customId and externalId.

This failsafe approach ensures session parameters are available every time at the start of the conversation.

This helps avoid situations where the call to the SunCo action Get User isn't complete before the conversation starts, and the information is available for retrieval.

articles.name: Can I automate the CSV export to my AI agent reporting dashboard?
articles.title: Can I automate the CSV export to my AI agent reporting dashboard?
articles.body:
Question

I use the AI agent reporting dashboard and want to automate access to reporting data instead of downloading the Export CSV file manually.

I want to use this data for recurring analysis and reporting, such as sending aggregated AI agent metrics to another tool or service.

What options are available for retrieving this data automatically? For example:

  • Can I schedule CSV exports on a daily or weekly basis?
  • Is there an API that provides the same reporting data available through the dashboard export?
  • Is there another recommended way to access AI agent reporting data programmatically?

Answer

Yes. You can use the Data Export API to export AI agent reporting data including conversation-level detail as JSON files from a secured API endpoint.

Important notes:

  • The Data Export API updates once per day at midnight UTC (Coordinated Universal Time)
  • Requests to Data Export API endpoints use the same account-wide Zendesk API rate limit as other API traffic
  • When calling the Data Export API endpoint https://yoursubdomain.zendesk.com/ai-agents/api/data-export/v3/get-signed-urls you must pass the request headers botId, organizationId, authorization, and date. Use the generated token for the authorization header. You can only pass one date value
  • The returned signed file URLs from the Data Export API endpoint don't need the API token. The signature in the URL query string is the authentication
  • The returned file URL is a temporary signed link that expires one day after the request date. You must call the endpoint again to get a fresh link if it expires
  • Historical data is available back to January 1, 2024. Anything older requires contacting Zendesk Customer Support
  • Generating the API token and finding the org ID both require admin access
  • The export for a date only includes conversations that ended on the date specified based on UTC (Coordinated Universal Time)

articles.name: Inline images in Knowledge articles display as broken across all browsers
articles.title: Inline images in Knowledge articles display as broken across all browsers
articles.body:
Issue symptoms

Inline images in knowledge base articles display as broken links for all users, or don't display for anonymous users or end users.

This problem occurs when an article contains inline image attachments from another article that is:

  • Restricted to a specific group of users
  • In draft status
  • In archived status

Due to any of these reasons, the image displays as a broken link, followed by the image name:

Resolution steps

To fix this issue, follow the step corresponding to the article status:

  • If the article is restricted to a specific group of users, update the restriction settings
  • If the article is in draft status, publish the article
  • If the article is in an archived status, restore the article

Alternatively, download the attachments and upload them individually to each article or use the knowledge media library. This is the recommended approach.

To identify the location of the attachment in the original article:

  1. Inspect the individual element in the browser console and copy its unique numerical ID

  2. Run the following API call for article attachments:

    https://{{subdomain}}.zendesk.com/api/v2/help_center/articles/attachments/123456789.json

    Replace subdomain with yoursubdomain and the unique ID value with that of the original article inline attachment.

You'll receive the following response that retrieves the original article source:

{
"article_attachment": {
"id": 123456789,
"url": "https://subdomain.zendesk.com/api/v2/help_center/articles/attachments/123456789",
"article_id": 360001328736,
"display_file_name": "Screen Shot 2020-02.png",
"file_name": "Screen_Shot_2020-02.png",
"content_url": "https://subdomain.zendesk.com/hc/article_attachments/1233456789/Screen_Shot_2020-02.png",
"relative_path": "/hc/article_attachments/123456789/Screen_Shot_2020-02.png",
"content_type": "image/png",
"size": 218402,
"inline": true,
"created_at": "2020-02-30T16:30:33Z",
"updated_at": "2020-02-30T16:45:03Z"
}
}

After you identify the article's unique ID, add it to any knowledge base article editor and this returns the article, for example:

https://{{subdomain}}.zendesk.com/knowledge/articles/360001328736/en-us?brand_id=3149466

For more information, see Working with articles in the knowledge base.

articles.name: Editing and managing custom agents (EAP)
articles.title: Editing and managing custom agents (EAP)
articles.body:
Custom agents can be updated at any time.

What's my plan?
All Suites Team, Growth, Professional, Enterprise, or Enterprise Plus

Summary: ◀▼

You can edit, activate, deactivate, and delete custom agents that automate tasks using AI and predefined workflows. Activate agents when ready to use, deactivate them to pause without deleting, and delete agents you no longer need. Managing custom agents helps maintain and update automated customer support processes effectively.

Note: Custom agents are currently in an early access program (EAP). To participate, see Joining the Custom Agents EAP.
Custom agents use a combination of AI, user-defined procedures, and approved articles, tools, and custom actions to automate complex tasks and resolve customer issues. After custom agents are created, admins can take the following actions to manage custom agents and maintain their workflows:
  • Editing custom agents
  • Activating and deactivating custom agents
  • Deleting custom agents
Related resources:
  • Understanding custom agents in Zendesk
  • Creating and using custom agents in Zendesk

Editing custom agents

Custom agents can be updated at any time.

To edit a custom agent
  1. In Admin Center, click AI in the sidebar, then select Agent builder > Custom agents.
  2. Next to the custom agent you want to edit, click the options menu () and select Edit.
  3. Make the necessary changes.
  4. Click Save.

Activating and deactivating custom agents

Custom agents are inactive by default. When you're ready to use them, activate them. If you need to modify a custom agent or temporarily don't need it, you can deactivate custom agents. They can be re-activated at any time. If you want to permanently remove a custom agent, you can delete it.
Note: Action flows that have a hand off step connected to a custom agent will break if the custom agent is deactivated.
To activate or deactivate a custom agent
  1. In Admin Center, click AI in the sidebar, then select Agent builder > Custom agents.
  2. Next to the custom agent, click the options menu () and select Activate or Deactivate.

Deleting custom agents

If you no longer need a custom agent, you can delete it. If you might need the custom agent again in the future, you can deactivate it instead.

To delete a custom agent
  1. In Admin Center, click AI in the sidebar, then select Agent builder > Custom agents.
  2. Next to the custom agent, click the options menu () and select Delete.
  3. In the confirmation dialog, click Delete.

articles.name: Can I use AI suggestions to generate use cases for advanced email AI agents?
articles.title: Can I use AI suggestions to generate use cases for advanced email AI agents?
articles.body:
Question

I can't generate any suggestions for my email AI agent, and the error appears with ai agent does not have any conversations.

Can I use AI Suggestions to generate use cases for advanced email AI agents?

Answer

Yes. The ai agent does not have any conversations error is misleading. It's tied to the source you picked rather than to the channel or bot generation. With the default Report preset > Quick, the Source defaults to This AI agent and includes only messages that were classified as not understood.

This method queries only for conversations carrying not understood conversations, and when it finds none, it returns the ai agent does not have any conversations error. A bot with plenty of traffic but few not understood messages may encounter this error. A topic needs at least 5 conversations before it surfaces as a suggestion, so a small sample can return nothing even when the import succeeds.

For AI agents connected to email channels, switch the Report preset from Quick to Custom and set Source to Zendesk Support. That pulls historical email tickets from your Zendesk account that includes public comments only, no private notes, excludes messaging tickets, and you can raise the Conversations sample to 1000 or 2000 to include more tickets.

articles.name: Can AI agents answer general knowledge questions?
articles.title: Can AI agents answer general knowledge questions?
articles.body:
Question

Can my AI agent answer general knowledge questions or widely known facts that aren’t included in my connected knowledge sources?

Answer

No. AI agents in Zendesk answer questions using the use cases you configure and the knowledge sources you connect to your account.

If a user asks a general knowledge question, such as “What is the capital of France?”, and that information isn’t available in the connected knowledge sources, the AI agent typically won’t answer it as a supported fact. Instead, it may fall back to another configured behavior, such as the Technical Error Reply use case, or another response path it determines is more appropriate.

This behavior is intentional. The AI agent focuses on content from connected knowledge sources, including your Zendesk Help Center and external knowledge sources. The AI agent stays grounded in your approved support content rather than act as a general-purpose knowledge bot. It works best when answering questions about your products and features, guiding common troubleshooting steps, and surfacing relevant help center content from connected and accessible sources.

For more information, see Connecting knowledge sources to power generative replies in AI agents.

articles.name: Release notes through 2026-08-28
articles.title: Release notes through 2026-08-28
articles.body:
See the What's New section for an overview of what was released last month.

This week's release notes include:

  • Knowledge and AI agents
  • Contact Center
  • Mobile SDKs
  • Apps and integrations
  • Products with no updates this week

Knowledge and AI agents

AI Copilot Procedures

New:

  • Admins in the Knowledge Copilot EAP can now manage the "Automatically generate procedures" setting in Admin Center > AI > Knowledge, rather than from the procedures list.
  • The banner announcing AI-generated procedures is now pinned to the top of the procedures list and can be dismissed. The in-page toggle is replaced with a link to Admin Center AI knowledge settings.

AI Agents Insights

Fixed:

  • Fixed an issue where article recommendations were generated using the account locale instead of the brand's Help Center locale.

AI agents - Advanced

New:
  • Unprocessed messages are now flagged in the conversation logs. Users can now see which end-
    user messages the AI agent ignored while executing a previous process.
  • Agentic email: Emails with multiple procedure requests, or a knowledge question and a procedure request, can now be handled together within the same email, rather than being escalated to a human agent.

Knowledge in Agent Workspace

Fixed:

  • Fixed an issue where tags older than 60 days didn't appear in autocomplete when building a user segment, so admins can now select from any of their account's tags, not just recently used ones.

Knowledge Editor

New:
  • Renamed "Content freshness" to "Content coverage" on article-update recommendations in Copilot. This aligns the subtitle copy with the "Create an article" recommendation.
  • The animate accordion toggle provides a smooth panel transition using::details-content + intrinsic-size interpolation as a progressive CSS enhancement; unsupported browsers keep the native toggle. 
Fixed:
  • Article translations now automatically expand referenced content blocks before processing
  • Changes made to an article title are preserved instead of reverting to the previous version.
  • Fix callout spacing and icon resizing. The grid gap was leaking between content rows, and the icon wasn't respecting the configured size

Help Center

Fixed:
  • Improved article rendering performance by avoiding redundant HTML sanitization and parsing during page rendering.

Contact Center

New:

  • Contact Center now supports agents running Zendesk in multiple browser tabs. A call rings on all open tabs, but Zendesk creates only one ticket.
  • Agent first callbacks let customers leave the queue without losing their place; the system rings the agent first, then automatically dials the customer.
  • Agents can now accept or decline incoming calls directly from the browser notification, without switching back to the Zendesk tab, so they can keep working in other applications and still answer calls promptly. Notifications need to be enabled in the browser and in agent settings. See Configuring browser notifications.

Fixed:

  • Fixed an issue where pressing the pause or play media keys would trigger the ringtone, causing agents to hear it even if they were actively on a call.

Mobile SDKs

Android release 3.0.0

New:

  • Minimum API level is now 24 (Android 7.0). Applications integrating the SDK must target Android 7.0 or higher.
  • Removed the deprecated Messaging module. The Messaging module public APIs, deprecated since 2.0.0, have been removed. Use the Zendesk module public APIs instead.
  • Additional language support: Added support for Estonian, Croatian, Icelandic, Kurdish, Lithuanian, Latvian, Slovenian, Albanian, Serbian, and Urdu.
  • Reduced permissions: Removed the READ_EXTERNAL_STORAGE permission requirement from the SDK.
  • Image loading performance: The SDK reuses the same image loader instance across recompositions and in both XML and Compose components, reducing unnecessary image reloads.

Dependency Updates:

  • Coil updated to 3.4.0
  • Retrofit updated to 3.0
  • OkHttp BOM updated to 5.4.0
  • Jetpack Compose Bill of Materials (BOM) updated to 2026.08.00
  • Firebase BOM updated to 34.17.0

Apps and integrations

New:
  • Aktie Send (Support)
    • Sends approved WhatsApp template messages from the ticket sidebar, threads replies back to the ticket, and provides compliance controls and delivery tracking.
  • Public Comment Alert (Support) (paid)
    • Displays a confirmation modal before sending public replies, helping agents review recipients and comments before updating a ticket.
  • Article Import & Export (Support) (paid)
    • Imports and exports multiple Guide articles using CSV files, supporting bulk creation, editing, sorting, and overwriting by article ID.
  • Macro Import & Export (Support) (paid)
    • Imports and exports multiple Zendesk macros in CSV format, including bulk creation and modification using macro IDs.
  • All View Display (Support) (paid)
    • Removes the standard limit on displayed views and organizes shared, personal, and group views into switchable tabs.
  • Batch Email Sender (Support) (paid)
    • Builds user lists and sends bulk email by generating tickets, with a workflow for selecting recipients, senders, and responsible agents.
  • URL Opener (Support) (paid)
    • Adds up to two configurable URL buttons to the ticket window, using ticket and customer information as URL variables.
  • Atlas 2026 Edition (Theme)
    • A polished, product-oriented Guide theme designed for B2B SaaS, developer tools, fintech, and documentation-heavy organizations.
  • Primer (Theme)
    • An education-focused Guide theme with persistent sidebar navigation for organizing admissions, courses, tuition, and campus services.
  • Aisle (Theme)
    • A retail-focused Guide theme that keeps orders, tracking, returns, payments, sizing, and gift cards easy to navigate.
  • Reel (Theme)
    • A media and subscription-focused Guide theme for organizing streaming, devices, plans, billing, and account access content.
  • Anvil (Theme)
    • An industrial support theme emphasizing high-contrast navigation, readable reference codes, procedures, safety, maintenance, and technical specifications.
  • Pulse (Theme)
    • A healthcare-oriented theme for organizing appointments, records, billing, prescriptions, privacy, and account access.
  • Capitol (Theme)
    • A government-focused Guide theme for organizing permits, licensing, utilities, billing, records, and public-service requests.
  • Route (Theme)
    • A transit-inspired, high-contrast Guide theme with clear hierarchy and short reading paths.
  • DeveloperHub Docs(Support)
    • DeveloperHub is a documentation platform that helps software companies write, publish, and maintain product documentation, API references, developer guides, and knowledge bases from one place. DeveloperHub Docs brings that same published documentation into Zendesk Support, so agents can answer tickets with the exact page a customer needs.
  • AI Ticket Tagger (Support)
    • AI Ticket Tagger reads the subject and description of the ticket you have open and suggests the most relevant tags from your own custom tag categories, right in the ticket sidebar.
  • Kai (Support)
    • Kai connects Kai’s AI platform with Zendesk so authorized users can create and route support tickets.
  • GetSupportClarity (Support)
    • Converts Zendesk activity into operational dashboards, leadership scorecards, AI-assisted summaries, drilldowns, exports, and synchronization-health reviews.
  • Zendesk Migration (Support)
    • Provides guided, secure, self-service migration of supported Freshdesk data and ticket history into Zendesk.
  • LaunchBrightly (Support)
    • LaunchBrightly eliminates the manual effort of keeping product screenshots up to date in your Zendesk Help Center. LaunchBrightly automates product screenshots by capturing authenticated application views, applying styling and annotations, and generating variants for different devices, themes, and languages.
  • Ticket Search & Export (Support) (paid)
    • Searches tickets using keywords, custom fields, and advanced filters, then exports ticket data and comments to CSV.
  • User Search & Export (Support) (paid)
    • Searches users by keywords, profile information, or tags, lets agents customize result columns, and exports results as CSV.
  • Snipzilla Templates (Support) (paid)
    • Provides reusable canned responses with smart tokens, prompts, folders, suggestions, macro import/export, and usage analytics.
  • Ticket Printer (Support)
    • Ticket Printer gives Zendesk Support agents control over what appears in a printed ticket record. Choose ticket and custom fields, then include the first, latest, all, or individually selected comments. Filter the conversation by public replies, internal notes, or specific commenters.

articles.name: Where can I find the Connect Instance ARN (Amazon Resource Name)?
articles.title: Where can I find the Connect Instance ARN (Amazon Resource Name)?
articles.body:
Question

Zendesk Contact Center uses Amazon Connect as its underlying telephony service. In some cases, the Zendesk Support team may need to contact AWS Support for assistance with your Amazon Connect configuration. When contacting AWS Support, you may be asked to provide your Amazon Connect instance Amazon Resource Name (ARN).

Where can I find the Connect Instance ARN?

Answer

Admins can access AWS Console from Contact Center to manage telephony and infrastructure settings.

To access the AWS Console:

  1. Click the Zendesk product menu in the top bar, then select Contact Center
  2. Under Overview, review your Amazon Connect instance details
  3. Click AWS Console to open the related AWS service

To find your Amazon Connect instance ARN in the AWS Console:

  1. Go to the Amazon Connect service
  2. On the Instances page, find your instance in the list
  3. Click the instance alias (the name you gave it during setup) to open its details page
  4. On the instance's Overview or details page, look for the Instance ARN field. It's displayed near the top, formatted as arn:aws:connect:<region>:<account-id>:instance/<instance-id>.

articles.name: Service Incident - August 19, 2026 - Support | Multiple Pods - App errors and timeouts
articles.title: Service Incident - August 19, 2026 - Support | Multiple Pods - App errors and timeouts
articles.body:
Summary

On August 19, 2026 from 6:27 UTC to 8:09 UTC, some Support customers using third party apps experienced errors and difficulties accessing those applications. The issue affected customers in several pods and resulted in 503 errors or timeouts.

Timeline

August 19, 2026 08:00 AM UTC | 1:00AM PT
 
We’re investigating an issue affecting third-party app functionality, where some customers may be unable to use certain apps or may encounter errors and timeouts. Our teams have observed that service is now operating normally. Please refresh your browser and check whether the issue has been resolved on your end. Thank you for your patience as we worked through this.
 
 
August 19, 2026 08:33 AM UTC | 1:33AM PT
 
We’re happy to report that the issue affecting third-party app functionality has been fully resolved and service has been restored. We appreciate your understanding and cooperation throughout this incident.

Root Cause Analysis

This incident was caused by a front-end change that unintentionally deprecated a feature flag which controlled routing for requests from applications, causing those requests to result in errors.

Resolution

To fix this issue, the feature flag was manually re-enabled, which restored application request routing to its intended path.

Remediation Items

  1. Change feature flag deprecation controls.
  2. Revisit and improve feature flag adjustment permissions.
  3. Improve runbook for similar deploys to reduce response time in similar scenarios.

FOR MORE INFORMATION

For current system status information about Zendesk and specific impacts to your account, visit our system status page. If you have additional questions about this incident, contact Zendesk customer support.

articles.name: Managing usage notifications for automated resolutions and resolution allowances
articles.title: Managing usage notifications for automated resolutions and resolution allowances
articles.body:
To help you manage automated resolutions or resolution allowance usage, you can configure the email notifications that admins receive to track usage. These notification settings work for usage tracked by theAutomated resolutions dashboardas well as usage tracked by theResolution allowanceandResolution usagedashboards.

What's my plan?
All Suites Team, Growth, Professional, Enterprise, or Enterprise Plus

Summary: ◀▼

Set up email notifications for automated resolutions and resolution allowances. Control which admins receive the notifications. Notifications help you stay informed about usage thresholds and forecasted overages, preventing unexpected charges.

Location: Admin Center > Account > Usage > Manage notifications

To help you manage automated resolutions or resolution allowance usage, you can configure the email notifications that admins receive to track usage. These notification settings work for usage tracked by the Automated resolutions dashboard as well as usage tracked by the Resolution allowance and Resolution usage dashboards.

This article contains these sections:

  • About configuring usage notification emails
  • Accessing the Manage notifications page

About configuring usage notification emails

You can configure email notifications to be sent when the following usage allowance events occur for automated resolutions and resolution allowances:

  • Approaching limit: Usage reaches a certain percentage of your overall resolution allowance. Options you can set range from 50% to 90%.
  • Reached limit: Usage reaches 100%.
  • Exceeding limit: Usage goes beyond 100%. Email notifications are sent at intervals of 10%.
  • Forecast: When the forecast indicates account usage may exceed the allowance.

For each notification type, you can configure which admins in your account will receive the email notifications.

Accessing the Manage notifications page

Use the Manage notifications page in Admin Center to set up email notifications for automated resolutions and resolution allowance usage.

To open the Manage notifications page

  • In Admin Center, click Account in the sidebar, then select Usage > Manage notifications.

    The Manage notifications page appears with a list of notification types. Use this page to configure recipients for each notification type.

Setting email notifications

For each notification type, you can configure which admins will receive an email notification. By default all admins in your account are included in the recipient list.

To set email notifications

  1. In Admin Center, click Account in the sidebar, then select Usage > Manage notifications.
  2. Click one of the following notification types to expand it: Approaching limit, Reached limit, Exceeding limit, or Forecast
  3. If you're setting the Approaching limit, click Send notification when usage reaches and select the desired percentage.

    You can set email notifications for one of the following: 50%, 60%, 70%, 80% or 90%.

    This setting applies only to the approaching limit. It's not applicable to the other notification types.

  4. Select the recipients to receive the email notification. See Adding or removing admins from the recipient list.
  5. When you’ve finished selecting recipients, click Save.

Adding or removing admins from the recipient list

For each notification type, you can select which admins will receive the notification. By default, all the current admins in your account are automatically included as recipients for all notification types, but any new admins you add going forward will need to be added manually. Only admins can be recipients of resolution allowance notifications.

Removing recipients

You can remove admins from the list, but at minimum, the account owner and at least one billing admin must be recipients.

To remove an admin from the list

  1. In Admin Center, click Account in the sidebar, then select Usage > Manage notifications.
  2. Click to expand the notification type you want to update.
  3. In the Recipient list, locate the admin you want to remove from the list.
  4. Click the options menu icon () next to the recipient and select Remove recipient.

  5. Continue to remove additional admins as needed.
  6. Click Save.

Adding recipients to a notification type

In some cases, you may want to add a previously-removed admin back into the recipient list or include a new admin you’re added recently to your account. New admins are not added automatically as notification recipients.

To add an admin to the list

  1. In Admin Center, click Account in the sidebar, then select Usage > Manage notifications.
  2. Click to expand the notification type you want to update.
  3. Scroll to the bottom of the recipient list and click Add recipient.

  4. Search to locate the admin you want to add, then click Add recipient.

    You can add one recipient at a time.

  5. Click Save.

Adding a recipient to all notifications

In some cases you might want to quickly add an admin to all notifications at once.

To add an admin to all notifications at once

  1. In Admin Center, click Account in the sidebar, then select Usage > Manage notifications.
  2. Click the Action menu at the top of the Manage notifications page.

  3. Select Add recipient to all notifications.
  4. Search to locate the admin you want to add, then click Add recipient.

    A confirmation message appears that says: "A recipient was added to all notifications."
